config.title: Barcelona
config.coverNote: I built this as a complete Barcelona week for two adults and children aged 5 and 9. I used JFK as the placeholder home airport, a family base in Poblenou, one principal outing each day, early dinners, and real room for a swim, a nap, or a change of mind. Every flight, table, transfer, activity, and confirmation number below is mocked for the prototype. Nothing is booked. If a plan needs to move, I move it.

days.title: Arrive gently
days.summary: Overnight flight, a private car, bags at the hotel, and an early dinner close to base.

days.title: Gaudí, then a quiet afternoon
days.summary: The Sagrada Família in the morning, a proper reset after lunch, and dinner early enough for everyone.

days.title: Park Güell and Gràcia
days.summary: One big visual morning, then the neighborhood and the hotel pool do the rest.

days.title: The science day
days.summary: CosmoCaixa gives the children something to touch and ask questions about, with no second major attraction attached.

days.title: Sand, harbor, and tapas
days.summary: A low-pressure beach morning and a long lunch. The afternoon is deliberately blank.

days.title: A little bit of magic
days.summary: Tibidabo as the one bigger family day, with the final dinner kept easy.

days.title: Home
days.summary: Breakfast, a pre-arranged car, and one last look at the city before the flight home.

picks.name: Sagrada Família
picks.description: The Gaudí landmark I would keep for the first full morning.
picks.note: The children do not need a lecture about the architecture. Let them look up, find animals in the stone, and choose one detail to remember. In this mock trip, I used the 10:00 AM entry.

picks.name: Park Güell
picks.description: A short, visual morning rather than an all-day march.
picks.note: Use the early slot and leave while it still feels fun. The mosaic dragon is the hook, but the real win is giving the children room to notice things on their own.

picks.name: CosmoCaixa Barcelona
picks.description: A hands-on science museum for a lower-pressure family day.
picks.note: This is a good counterweight to churches and plazas. The five-year-old can touch and watch things happen, while the nine-year-old gets enough explanation to stay with it.

picks.name: Tibidabo
picks.description: The bigger family day, held for the end of the trip.
picks.note: Before a real booking I would check height rules and the operating calendar. For this mock, it is the one day where the adults can be children too.

picks.name: Barceloneta Beach
picks.address: Passeig Marítim de la Barceloneta, 08003 Barcelona
picks.description: An easy weather-dependent morning with no ticket attached.
picks.note: Bring hats, a change of clothes, and sealed snacks. Keep the water optional and let the morning stay small.

picks.name: La Mar Salada
picks.address: Passeig de Joan de Borbó 58-59, 08003 Barcelona
picks.description: Seafood near the water, used here as the long lunch anchor.
picks.note: This is where I would let lunch stretch. The afternoon is intentionally blank, so there is no reason to rush the last plate.

picks.name: Bodega Joan
picks.description: A straightforward tapas table that works well early.
picks.note: I used this twice in the mock because repetition is useful with children. Familiar menus are not a failure of imagination. They are how everyone gets to dinner in a good mood.

picks.name: Cuines Santa Caterina
picks.address: Mercat de Santa Caterina, Avinguda de Francesc Cambó 16, 08003 Barcelona
picks.description: Market-hall flexibility for a family that wants different things.
picks.note: This is the useful kind of restaurant on a family trip. Everyone can find something, nobody has to pretend to like the same thing, and the room still feels like Barcelona.

picks.name: El Nacional
picks.description: A large room with several food counters and an early family table.
picks.note: I like this when the group has different appetites. It gives the adults a proper setting without turning dinner into a negotiation.

picks.name: Granja M. Viader
picks.description: A classic breakfast stop for hot chocolate and pastries.
picks.note: I would go early, order for the table, and let this be the first story the children tell about the city.

picks.name: Hofmann Pastisseria
picks.description: A pastry stop before the science museum morning.
picks.note: One good pastry is enough. I would keep it simple and make the walk afterward part of the morning.

picks.name: Barcelona Aquarium
picks.address: Moll d’Espanya del Port Vell, 08039 Barcelona
picks.description: A practical rainy-day alternative to the beach.
picks.note: I kept this as the weather backup rather than adding it to the main week. A good family trip needs an escape hatch, not more commitments.

picks.name: Laie bookstore at CaixaForum
picks.address: Av. Francesc Ferrer i Guàrdia 6-8, 08038 Barcelona
picks.description: A small book stop to keep in reserve near Montjuïc.
picks.note: If the children want a souvenir, I would choose a book before another plastic object. It travels home better.

guideBlocks.heading: Prototype status
guideBlocks.body: This is a complete mocked Carta for a family of four. The flight numbers, confirmation codes, hotel stay, restaurant tables, activity entries, and provider contacts are placeholders. No money has moved, no inventory has been checked, and no reservation exists.

guideBlocks.heading: How I shaped the week
guideBlocks.body: The five and nine-year-old get one principal outing each day, protected rest windows after lunch, and early dinners. The optional places stay in Picks so the family can add them only when everyone still has energy.

guideBlocks.heading: Working assumptions
guideBlocks.body: I used October 14 to 20, 2026, JFK as the placeholder home airport, Poblenou as the base, and two child restraints requested for every private transfer. Before this becomes a real trip, I would confirm names, passport details, children’s heights and weights, room configuration, flight origin, operating calendars, and the actual restaurant availability.

guideBlocks.heading: Moving around with children
guideBlocks.body: Use walking for the neighborhood days and a private car for the airport and Tibidabo. For every real transfer, confirm the correct restraint for each child in writing. If the children are done, remove the next optional stop. The schedule is designed to survive that decision.

guideBlocks.heading: Food and dinner timing
guideBlocks.body: No allergy or dietary restriction was provided, so the mock uses flexible restaurants and early tables. If there is an allergy, tell me before booking. I would attach it to every reservation and confirm ingredients, sauces, oils, preparation surfaces, and cross-contact handling with a manager.

guideBlocks.heading: Power and plug compatibility
guideBlocks.body: Spain uses Type C and Type F outlets at 230V and 50Hz. Pack one compact European adapter in the carry-on. Most modern phone, laptop, and camera chargers accept 100 to 240V, but hair tools and specialty devices often do not, so check their labels before bringing them.
